response.text:
Targets already used during fitting make pseudo-holdout perturbations diagnostics of fitted-model reliance, not unbiased predictive generalization. Removing a target from the diagnostic input does not erase its training influence. Generalization claims require target events genuinely excluded from fitting and selection, with histories restricted to preceding interactions; the item itself may still appear in other users’ training histories. Global temporal boundaries additionally prevent future-interaction leakage. [Time to Split](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.16289) documents how splitting choices change sequential-model rankings.

Recommended controlled protocol: freeze weights, disable dropout, and compare equal-count recent versus old deletions on identical eligible users, reporting whether recent deletion includes the final item. Run two distinct interventions: position-preserving masking removes item evidence while retaining surviving positions; compaction also changes positional distances and adjacency. Verify actual attention-mask behavior and keep the prediction query/readout fixed; an untrained mask token introduces distribution shift. Shuffle only earlier valid items while preserving the last item, item multiset, length and padding, using repeated seeded permutations. This probes sensitivity to earlier ordering conditional on the final interaction; a small effect does not establish that temporal information is unnecessary. These are experimental-design recommendations, not a universally validated diagnostic standard.

Keep each user’s target, 99 unique negatives, exclusions and tie-breaking identical across conditions; never regenerate candidates from perturbed histories. Sampled HR remains candidate-dependent and cannot establish full-catalog performance ([sampling analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.02263)). Report paired per-user HR@10 differences and 95% user-bootstrap intervals, resampling within category before macro-averaging; aggregate repeated perturbations within user rather than treating them as independent samples. Separate perturbation randomness from training-seed variability. [Inference at Scale](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.02461) supports bootstrap and randomization-based inference. Such intervals quantify sensitivity uncertainty; they cannot correct target contamination or establish causal user preferences.
